text.p: Swiss engineering group Sulzer AG said on Thursday its 1996 group net profit is likely to be lower than that of 1995 due to an unexpected appeals court ruling in the U.S. ordering its Intermedics Inc unit to pay $73 million in connection with a patent suit.
Sulzer was ordered to pay the $73 million last year as the result of a patent dispute with Stryker Corp.
Sulzer said at the start of this month that provisions had been set aside, but the potential damages in connection with the case remained uncertain.
Sulzer said in its statement that the provisions set aside earlier to cover the suit should its appeal fail amounted to 45 million Swiss francs.
Therefore the group's 1996 results would be hit by an extraordinary charge of an additional 45 million francs as a result of the court ruling.

A Sulzer spokesman said in response to an inquiry that although the initial court decision was for damages of $73 million (or about 90 million francs), the company believed there was a good chance that the damages would be reduced on appeal.
